tasks.short: Brief workers on work-area radiation levels

steps.what: Read the actual work-area survey and locate the applicable area and survey-version references
Brief the actual workers on area radiation levels and clarify their questions

tasks.design: Link current survey references by area in {OTHER}, the radiation survey system, with controlled pages in {DOCS}. The technician still reads the actual survey, checks its relevance and briefs the workers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating the applicable area survey could require repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native area and survey-version links can remove navigation without interpreting exposure conditions.
tasks.still_hard: Workers need to understand the actual area's conditions and uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: The technician explains the context and checks that questions are understood.

ambition.what: No expanded radiation-work or access authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: area-linked survey references can shorten retrieval while radiation briefings remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is an actual oral radiation-level briefing, not a work permit or access authorization. No trailing briefing report is invented where none is kept.

The existing survey comes from actual radiation-monitoring work, not a new free feed; s1 counts technician verification of area, survey date, measurement units and version. Shared survey production is counted in its actual monitoring task once.

Any actual written worker notice or operative clearance needs its real authority and separate final-version action. Shares are unmeasured activity estimates.
unknowns: Actual briefing route and record requirements
research_questions: Does the native area link remove an actual repeated search?

already_counted.description: Actual survey reading, verification and worker briefing remain counted.

tasks.short: Inform supervisors of exposures approaching limits

steps.what: Read actual individual or area measurements and identify their units, periods and applicable approved limits
Compare selected actual exposure and area readings against the fixed applicable approach thresholds
Verify actual identity, timing and measurement reliability and judge the reporting significance
Inform the actual supervisor promptly and clarify the exposure or area-level concern

tasks.design: Configure a fixed threshold-comparison view in {OTHER}, the radiation monitoring and dosimetry system, using the applicable approved references in {DOCS}. The technician verifies the actual context and informs the supervisor directly; the helper does not replace alarms or delay urgent reporting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some cumulative or cross-record comparisons could be done manually outside existing alarm views.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed unit, period and limit fields can support explicit arithmetic without a model.
tasks.still_hard: A comparison is meaningful only with the correct person, area, period and reliable measurement.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognizes significance and communicates promptly under the actual procedure.

ambition.what: No new exposure-limit or response authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed measurement and period fields can be compared against approved thresholds while reporting significance and supervisor communication remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is the actual supervisor notification episode. No written incident report is invented for an oral notification; an actual written report, if required, needs its real writing and separate final-version send.

Measurements originate in real monitoring work. The technician identifies person or area, time period, unit, value and applicable approved threshold in s1; missing or inconsistent inputs remain manual.

Test current native threshold views first. Existing alarms and automatic comparisons earn zero new saving. The estimate applies only to an actual currently manual cross-record comparison, not an invented replacement for already automatic alarms.
s2 creates a draft comparison view, not an autonomous notification or equipment response. Actual urgent reporting is not conditional on this helper being available.
Shares are unmeasured episode estimates and upstream measurement capture is counted once in its actual task.

already_counted.description: Input verification, significance judgment and actual prompt supervisor communication remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain approved threshold mappings and unit/period test fixtures.

tasks.short: Provide the initial response to abnormal radiation events

steps.what: Read the actual alarm indications and locate the applicable abnormal-event reference
Assess the actual event and determine the specific initial response under the procedure
Check current response readiness and authorize the exact action within actual delegated response authority
Carry out the exact initial on-site response under the actual procedure
Verify the actual immediate outcome and unresolved abnormal conditions
Write the actual event-response log entry used by the duty radiation-protection team
Save the ordinary event-response entry in the same log

tasks.design: Link current abnormal-event references in {DOCS} to the actual alarm context in {OTHER}, the radiation monitoring system. Keep assessment, live response readiness, initial action, outcome verification and the real event-response log with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating the applicable reference could require a separate search after reading the alarm.
tasks.enabler_now: Native equipment and reference-version links can remove a small navigation component.
tasks.still_hard: Initial response depends on live conditions and the actual procedure, not generic generated advice.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognizes the event and acts within real response authority.

ambition.what: No autonomous event response or expanded authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: equipment-linked references can support human response preparation without controlling a radiation response.

assumptions: This is an actual on-site initial-response episode with an existing event-response log used by the duty radiation-protection team. No new report or self-approval is added.

The technician checks alarm identity and current reference in s1. The intended action exists in s2 before current readiness in s3; actual delegated authority must be verified, otherwise use and count the actual authority.
a1 gates the real on-site response action, not authored paperwork. Any action or current-condition change voids it. No automated response is proposed and urgent action must not wait for a helper.

tasks.short: Teach radiation safety and demonstrate protective equipment

steps.what: Read the actual current radiation-safety procedure and locate the protective-equipment instruction
Instruct the actual personnel in applicable radiation-safety procedures and answer questions
Physically demonstrate actual protective clothing and equipment use and observe personnel practice
Enter the actual training date, attendance and topics in the existing training log used for refresher planning
Save the ordinary factual training entry in the same learning system

tasks.design: Bookmark the current equipment-specific instruction in {DOCS}. Keep live instruction, physical demonstration and the actual factual attendance entry in {LMS} with the technician; {OTHER} denotes the real protective equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: The specific equipment instruction could require navigation within the current procedure set.
tasks.enabler_now: A native version-aware bookmark can remove only that small retrieval component.
tasks.still_hard: Correct practical use requires physical demonstration and observation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognizes misunderstood safety instructions and incorrect equipment use.

ambition.what: No new qualification or access-grant authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: current-reference bookmarks can shorten retrieval but do not replace practical radiation-safety instruction.

assumptions: Episode is real radiation-safety instruction with the facility's existing factual training log used for refresher planning. Do not add a log to an informal demonstration if none is kept.
The technician reads the actual procedure in s1 and observes actual participation in s2-s3 before entering date, participant identifier and taught topics in s4. No free structured attendance feed.
The bookmark removes0.5 of10 retrieval/reading units;9.5 remain for actual source reading. Test current native bookmarks first; already available retrieval earns zero new gain.
